questions.question: Define electrolysis, and compare galvanic and electrolytic cells under three headings: energy conversion, spontaneity, and electrode polarity. State which definitions stay the same in both cell types.
questions.expected_answer: Electrolysis is the chemical process in which electrical energy is used to drive a non-spontaneous redox reaction. Comparison: (1) Energy conversion — a galvanic cell converts chemical energy to electrical energy; an electrolytic cell converts electrical energy to chemical energy. (2) Spontaneity — the galvanic cell's reaction is spontaneous; the electrolytic cell's reaction is non-spontaneous and must be forced by an external power source. (3) Polarity — in a galvanic cell the anode is negative and the cathode positive; in an electrolytic cell the anode is positive (wired to the positive terminal) and the cathode negative. Unchanged in both: oxidation always occurs at the anode, reduction always occurs at the cathode, the electrolyte conducts through the movement of ions, anions migrate toward the anode and cations toward the cathode.

questions.question: For the electrolysis of a copper(II) chloride solution with carbon electrodes: give the half-reaction and observation at each electrode, the net reaction, and explain why the solution's colour fades. Then give the electrode arrangement and electrolyte needed to silver-plate a steel spoon.
questions.expected_answer: Cathode (negative): Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Cu; observation — a salmon-brown layer of copper metal deposits on the electrode. Anode (positive): 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻; observation — bubbles of chlorine gas with a sharp chlorine smell. Net reaction: Cu²⁺ + 2Cl⁻ → Cu + Cl₂; the compound is decomposed into its elements using electrical energy (carbon electrodes are inert and take no part). The blue-green colour fades because Cu²⁺ ions, which cause the colour, are progressively removed from solution as copper plates onto the cathode. Silver plating: the spoon is the cathode (connected to the negative terminal), a bar of silver is the anode, and the electrolyte is a solution of silver ions such as silver nitrate. At the anode Ag → Ag⁺ + e⁻ (the bar dissolves, replenishing the bath); at the cathode Ag⁺ + e⁻ → Ag (silver deposits on the spoon). Plating is done for protection against corrosion and for appearance.

questions.question: For the electrolysis of concentrated sodium chloride solution: give the half-reaction at each electrode, explain why hydrogen rather than sodium forms at the cathode and why the solution must be concentrated, name the three products, and give one use of each.
questions.expected_answer: Anode: 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻ (chlorine gas). Cathode: 2H₂O + 2e⁻ → H₂ + 2OH⁻ (hydrogen gas). Sodium ions are extremely difficult to reduce — sodium is one of the strongest reducing agents, so its ion clings to the ionised state — and water is reduced preferentially, producing hydrogen and hydroxide ions; the Na⁺ ions remain in solution and, with the OH⁻ ions formed, constitute sodium hydroxide. The solution must be concentrated because in dilute solution water out-competes chloride at the anode and oxygen forms instead of chlorine; the high chloride concentration ensures chlorine is the anode product. Products and uses: chlorine — purification of drinking and pool water, bleach, PVC manufacture; hydrogen — fuel, hardening of oils, ammonia synthesis; sodium hydroxide (caustic soda) — making soap, paper and textiles.
